working_resolution.note: every image is resized to px_per_m (measured from the red marker); hold_scale multiplies the size limits below (1.0 = a ~22 px hold)

candidates.note: fixed for every algorithm; the per-algorithm values (superpixel size, contrast threshold, saturation floor) are picked by the sweep and stored in algorithms.json

marker.note: 1 m on walls at least 2 m wide, 0.1 m on narrower ones; scene.json states it

grid.note: real walls: calibration from the bolt-hole grid (20 cm, from the handout); dot sizes are for photos ~1280 px wide; tolerance and reach are in grid cells

real_walls.note: photos are resized so a typical real hold (hold_size_m) is as many pixels as a synthetic hold (synthetic_hold_size_m) at the working resolution, so the synthetic pixel settings keep their meaning; real_shape = size/shape limits for real holds (the synthetic ones fit only the simulator's single hold model)

yaw.note: template = silhouette of template_source at yaw 0 (excluded from the yaw scores)

stereo.note: z from stereo only if its expected depth error is below max_z_sigma_m, otherwise z = 0
